newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CPN FUEL DISTRIBUTOR RAISES PRICES MARCH 3.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CPN FUEL DISTRIBUTOR RAISES PRICES MARCH 3.

text.p: Poland's largest fuel distributor, the state-owned Centrala Produktow Naftowych SA (CPN), will raise petrol prices on March 3, Gazeta Wyborcza newspaper said on Saturday.
The newspaper quoted CPN senior official Jan Paczkowski as saying the move aimed at bringing prices of domestically produced fuels closer to those of imported petrol.
The raise by three groszes per litre for all types of petrol is the second price increase since February 14, when fuel prices were freed from all government control.
The finance ministry had earlier controlled maximum prices of domestically produced-fuel and distributors' margins on imported and domestic fuel.
Gazeta Wyborcza said the price of 95 octane unleaded petrol would rise to 1.58 zlotys per litre from 1.55 zlotys, the 98 octane unleaded petrol would cost 1.76 zlotys.
The price of the 94 octane leaded petrol would increase to 1.62 zlotys and the price of the 98 octane leaded petrol would go up to 1.78 zlotys.
In 1996, CPN had 1,365 filling stations out of Poland's about 4,800 stations.
It has a 50 percent share of Poland's petrol and diesel fuel retail market.
